title: Terraform admin roles, admin users and local users in ZIA

checks.do: Whether a plan that changes `role_type` on an existing admin role failed on the immutability check, which needs a destroy and recreate.
Whether an SDWAN role sets `policy_access` to READ_WRITE and `alerting_access` to NONE before suspecting the API.
Whether an imported API-only role declares `role_type = "PUBLIC_API"` directly rather than ignoring the attribute.
Whether a user plan that shows name or email drift on a Zidentity-migrated tenant runs a provider older than v4.7.24.
Whether a password or auth-method difference is expected, since neither is refreshed from ZIA on read.

role-type-values.statement: The `role_type` validator on `zia_admin_roles` accepts ORG_ADMIN, EXEC_INSIGHT, EXEC_INSIGHT_AND_ORG_ADMIN, SDWAN and PUBLIC_API, so a role can declare PUBLIC_API in HCL without failing validation.

role-type-immutable.statement: A plan-time check rejects any change to `role_type` once the `zia_admin_roles` resource has an ID, with the error "the role_type cannot be changed once the resource is created"; so a role's type cannot be changed in place.

quotes: the role_type cannot be changed once the resource is created. old=%v new=%v

sdwan-role-constraints.statement: When `role_type` is SDWAN, the same plan-time check requires `policy_access` to be READ_WRITE and `alerting_access` to be NONE, and fails the plan otherwise.

quotes: for SDWAN roles, policy_access must be READ_WRITE
for SDWAN roles, alerting_access must be NONE

rank-unvalidated.statement: The `rank` attribute of `zia_admin_roles` is an optional integer with no range validator in the schema; its description gives 7 as the default and lowest rank and says it applies only when admin rank is enabled in Advanced Settings.

quotes: This is applicable only when admin rank is enabled in the advanced settings.

admin-password-not-returned.statement: The `zia_admin_users` password is sensitive, is mandatory for creation when admin single sign-on is disabled, and the schema says the API does not provide it in a GET response.

quotes: If admin single sign-on (SSO) is disabled, then this field is mandatory for POST requests.
This information is not provided in a GET response.

user-read-sets-no-password.statement: The `zia_user_management` Read copies name, email, comments, temp_auth_email, groups and department from the response into state and sets neither `password` nor `auth_methods`, so the configured password is never refreshed from ZIA.

quotes: if err := d.Set("department", flattenUserDepartment(resp.Department)); err != nil {

user-read-from-list.statement: Since provider v4.7.24 the `zia_user_management` Read resolves the user from the list endpoint (name-filtered first, then a full list scan) instead of the per-ID lookup, because on Zidentity-migrated tenants the per-ID lookup returns name and email in an encoded form that produced a perpetual in-place update on every plan.

quotes: Fixed the `zia_user_management` resource to read the user's `name` and `email` from the user list instead of the single-user lookup.
// Resolve the user from the list endpoint rather than the per-ID endpoint.
the lookup falls back to an unfiltered list scan

user-email-unique.statement: The provider documents that a user email need not be a valid address but must be unique and its domain must belong to the organization.

quotes: it must be unique and its domain must belong to the organization

rank-values-fixed.title: Whether admin rank values are fixed ZIA system values rather than organization-specific
rank-values-fixed.detail: Unverified legacy statement: admin rank values are fixed ZIA system values, not organization-specific. The provider schema has no range validator and the help captures describe rank only as a hierarchy, so neither settles whether a tenant can define its own rank values.
rank-values-fixed.blocks: saying whether a rank number means the same thing in every tenant
